chunks: What al-Shaykh, may Allah Most High support him, informed me of, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from his father, from al-Ḥusayn ibn al-Ḥasan ibn Abān, from al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr and Faḍālah, from Jamīl ibn Darrāj, from Zurārah ibn Aʿyan, who said:

Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام described to us the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم. He called for a vessel of water, then inserted his right hand and took a handful of water, and let it flow over his face from the top of the face. Then he wiped the two eyebrows together with his hand. Then he returned the left hand into the vessel and let it flow over the right arm, then wiped its sides. Then he returned the right hand into the vessel, then poured it over the left arm and did with it as he had done with the right. Then he wiped, with the remainder of what remained in his two hands, his head and his feet, and he did not return them into the vessel.
As for his statement, 'and he does not face the hair of his forearms,' its indication is clear.

key_terms.الْإِنَاءِ: the vessel containing the water used for wudu
key_terms.الْيُسْرَى: the left hand or left arm, washed after the right
key_terms.الْيُمْنَى: the right hand or right arm, used first in the sequence
key_terms.رَأْسَهُ: his head, which was wiped with remaining moisture
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم, whose practice is being narrated
key_terms.رِجْلَيْهِ: his feet, which were wiped with the remaining moisture
key_terms.وَجْهِهِ: his face, the first area washed in the description
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual purification being described

ai.seo_question: How is the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم described in this hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the manner of the wudu of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم as narrated by Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام. It outlines washing the face and arms, then wiping the head and feet with the remaining moisture in the hands, showing the transmitted prophetic practice in ritual purification.
